overview: The Medford School Committee serves as the governing body for Medford Public Schools, overseeing educational policy, district budgets, facilities, personnel contracts, and operational guidelines. The committee's recorded proceedings span from January 2020 through October 2026 across four successive terms. Throughout this timeframe, the committee managed pandemic remote learning and re-entry protocols, negotiated multi-year labor contracts across all employee units, responded to facility infrastructure failures, and transitioned executive leadership. At its most recent meetings, the committee has focused on selecting geothermal HVAC systems for elementary schools, expanding after-school program capacity, refining the Medford High School building project, and drafting a new district strategic plan.

threads.name: Medford High School building project
threads.summary: The committee initiated efforts to address aging infrastructure at Medford High School by authorizing the submission of Statements of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority [M35#9, M44#3, M46#1]. Following acceptance into the MSBA core program eligibility phase [M90#5], the committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee, approved its governance structure and project goals, and appointed voting and non-voting community members and municipal representatives [M93#6, M95#2, M95#7, M100#8]. The district selected Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager to oversee the feasibility study [M132#4, M139#5] and formally approved the project's educational specifications and plan [M156#3, M173#7]. The committee and building project team narrowed design alternatives to account for a 1967 deed restriction on Edgerly Field [M144#6, M165#3, M168#2, M171#3], while voting to pursue LEED v4 Silver certification and retain dedicated space for a Teen Health Center [M175#6, M175#7].

threads.name: School facilities condition and HVAC modernization
threads.summary: Prompted by recurring heating and cooling system failures across district schools [M82#6], the committee approved a $15 to $20 million decarbonization scope for HVAC systems at the Andrews and McGlynn schools [M102#6] and adopted a policy restricting future purchases of fossil-fuel powered facility equipment [M102#13]. The body subsequently authorized construction management at risk delivery and bond requests totaling over $25 million to execute HVAC and roof replacements at both schools [M123#6, M127#6, M136#7], alongside a solar power purchase agreement [M152#4]. The district received a comprehensive facilities assessment identifying $83.7 million in required repairs across five schools [M150#3] and approved updated multi-year capital plans [M127#8, M153#6, M158#7]. The committee also advanced MSBA Accelerated Repair projects for elementary schools, approving air-to-water heat pump and roof schematic designs for Roberts Elementary [M134#1, M173#5, M176#4, M180#5] and selecting a ground-source geothermal heat pump system for Missituk Elementary [M180#4].

threads.name: Collective bargaining and labor agreements
threads.summary: The committee regularly negotiates and ratifies collective bargaining agreements across ten district employee bargaining units. Negotiations with the Medford Teachers Association faced state mediation, impasses, and a failed initial ratification vote [M48#8, M53#5, M58#3, M62#6] before a four-year agreement was ratified [M63#5], followed later by a successor three-year contract adding instructional time to the school day [M138#3]. The committee also approved multi-year agreements and memoranda for paraprofessionals and Kids Corner employees [M17#9, M56#2, M111#2, M111#3, M145#2], nurses [M54#1, M147#1], administrators [M84#1, M96#4, M141#6, M143#7], cafeteria workers [M107#2, M159#1], and custodial and clerical personnel [M108#2]. Ongoing labor responsibilities continue to involve executive session grievance and bargaining reviews [M169#2, M170#1, M177#1].

threads.name: Before and after school care operations and expansion
threads.summary: Faced with persistent waitlists and staffing shortages in elementary child care programs [M18#4, M62#4], the committee repeatedly approved tuition adjustments, staff pay increases, and lotteries to stabilize operations [M19#9, M38#6, M71#8, M96#7, M137#1]. The district partnered with City Year to provide classroom and after-school coverage [M108#4, M115#3] and authorized an operational review by the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) [M140#2]. Following BASIC's recommendations, the committee approved expanding program capacity by 150 seats, adjusting tuition rates, and elevating site coordinator roles to full-time positions [M145#3, M166#4, M166#5]. Subsequent program reports demonstrated a 68 percent reduction in waitlist numbers and a 50 percent increase in overall program enrollment [M177#5, M180#3].

threads.name: Elementary school enrollment, capacity, and redistricting
threads.summary: Early enrollment surges created localized capacity strains at elementary buildings [M33#5], developing by 2024 into acute overcrowding at Roberts Elementary where student enrollment exceeded 590 [M113#8, M114#6, M137#4]. To relieve immediate building congestion, the committee approved relocating preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary and formed a strategic space planning task force [M142#6, M142#7]. An external space utilization study recommended reconfiguring grade spans across the district, though the committee tabled the proposal and voted to delay any grade 5–8 middle school model until at least the 2028–2029 school year [M151#5, M152#5, M175#4]. The committee subsequently took up a proposed elementary school reassignment policy to formalize procedures and capacity buffers for alternative school placements [M179#5].

threads.name: District leadership and superintendent succession
threads.summary: The committee managed executive evaluations and contract terms for Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent over several annual review cycles [M19#6, M25#1, M76#6, M79#2, M91#8]. In mid-2024, the committee entered contract negotiations with the superintendent [M110#2, M112#2, M116#1, M117#1], leading to her announced departure in January 2025 [M127#3, M128#5, M128#9]. The committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent [M126#2, M128#3], who presented a transitional leadership plan and completed annual performance reviews [M129#2, M150#5, M154#4, M155#6]. In February 2026, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent, subsequently negotiating and approving a three-year contract [M156#4, M166#6, M177#6].

threads.name: School climate, safety protocols, and student discipline
threads.summary: Prompted by rising student behavioral concerns and suspension trends, the committee examined discipline data and initiated restorative justice pilot initiatives [M32#4, M32#12, M34#8, M37#5, M59#8]. A student stabbing at Medford High School led to special safety meetings, the introduction of a 10-point security plan, and the retention of consultant Michael Welch to evaluate high school culture and operations [M63#3, M63#4, M64#5, M64#6, M73#7]. The committee also updated incident reporting mechanisms [M64#8, M65#4] and revised the district's Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan policy [M80#6, M93#7]. Safety and disciplinary governance continued through regular suspension tracking reports [M97#12, M102#7, M143#13], high school bathroom security and vape detector investments [M122#7, M125#9], and updates to student handbooks and physical restraint policies [M167#6, M173#6].
